title: Remote six-hour counts gave no clear change around 286 isolated M7+ earthquakes in ComCat, 2000-2025
abstract: We tested remote catalog counts in the six hours before and after 286 isolated M7+ earthquakes in 2000-2025. Targets had preferred magnitude at least 5.5 and below 6.5 and distance greater than 2,000 km. There were 76 before counts and 53 after counts. The after-to-before ratio was 0.697. Its conditional 95% year-bootstrap interval was 0.453 to 1.066. The primary test did not resolve a count change. Two-year and three-year block intervals also included one. A larger deficit in the M7.5+ subset was a secondary result and did not pass a ten-test comparison rule. The count sign is compatible with missed detections, but does not identify that cause or a physical rate change. Selected isolated centers, mixed magnitude scales, sparse counts, catalog revisions and annual uncertainty assumptions limit inference. Code, aggregate counts, a figure, source hashes and an independent count audit support reproduction. Raw and event-level records stay outside the bundle.

display.caption: Count ratios and annual differences. Intervals resample center years. Secondary rows are unadjusted and do not establish a physical cause.

citations.reason: Published method evidence set separate center and target magnitude ranges. We reuse the same public source snapshot, with new code and a different remote-window question.
